Starts correctly at $L$ but then runs around the image triangle the wrong way — $M$ is the reflection of $F$, not of $E$.

questions.solution_text:
The reflection matches $D \leftrightarrow L$, $E \leftrightarrow K$ and $F \leftrightarrow M$.
$\triangle DEF \equiv \triangle LKM$

questions.question_text: In the statement $\triangle BDF \equiv \triangle HKM$, which vertex corresponds to $D$?

options.why: $H$ is the first-listed vertex, so it corresponds to $B$ — $D$ is the second-listed vertex of its triangle.
$M$ is the third-listed vertex, so it corresponds to $F$, not to the second-listed $D$.

questions.solution_text:
Matching the positions: $B \leftrightarrow H$, $D \leftrightarrow K$, $F \leftrightarrow M$.
$D$ corresponds to $K$.

questions.question_text:
$\triangle PRT \equiv \triangle CEG$.
Which side corresponds to side $PT$?

options.why: $CE$ joins the first two listed vertices, so it corresponds to $PR$ — $PT$ joins the first and third.
$EG$ joins the second and third listed vertices, so it corresponds to $RT$, not $PT$.

questions.solution_text:
$P \leftrightarrow C$ and $T \leftrightarrow G$.
Side $PT$ corresponds to side $CG$.

questions.question_text:
Quadrilateral $KLMN \equiv$ quadrilateral $WXYZ$.
Which angle corresponds to $\angle M$?

options.why: $\angle X$ is at the second-listed vertex, matching $\angle L$ — $M$ is the third-listed vertex.
$\angle Z$ is at the last-listed vertex, matching $\angle N$, not the third-listed $\angle M$.

questions.solution_text:
$M$ is the third-listed vertex, matching the third-listed vertex $Y$.
$\angle M$ corresponds to $\angle Y$.

questions.question_text: Given $\triangle GHK \equiv \triangle PQR$, which statement is also correct?

options.why: Re-orders the left side only, so $H$ is now paired with $P$ — but $H$ corresponds to $Q$; both sides must move together.
Pairs $H$ with $P$ in the middle positions, but $H$ corresponds to $Q$ — the second letters no longer match.
Swaps $K$ and $H$ on one side only, pairing $K$ with $Q$ instead of with $R$.

questions.solution_text:
Starting both sides one vertex later keeps every pair together: $H \leftrightarrow Q$, $K \leftrightarrow R$, $G \leftrightarrow P$.
$\triangle HKG \equiv \triangle QRP$ names the same correspondence.

questions.question_text:
$\triangle CDE \equiv \triangle WYX$, $\angle C = 71^{\circ}$ and $\angle D = 56^{\circ}$.
Find the size of $\angle WYX$.

options.why: $71^{\circ}$ is $\angle C$, which corresponds to $\angle W$ — but the vertex of $\angle WYX$ is its middle letter $Y$, which matches $D$.
$180^{\circ} - 71^{\circ} - 56^{\circ} = 53^{\circ}$ is the third angle $\angle E$, which corresponds to $\angle X$, not to the angle at $Y$.

questions.solution_text:
The vertex of $\angle WYX$ is its middle letter, $Y$.
$D \leftrightarrow Y$, so $\angle WYX = \angle D$.
$\angle WYX = 56^{\circ}$

questions.question_text:
Quadrilateral $DEFG \equiv$ quadrilateral $RSTU$, with $RS = 6$ cm, $ST = 9$ cm and $TU = 7$ cm.
Find the length of $EF$.

options.why: $6$ cm is $RS$, which corresponds to $DE$ — $E$ pairs with $S$ and $F$ with $T$, so $EF$ matches $ST$.
$7$ cm is $TU$, which corresponds to $FG$, the next side around, not to $EF$.

questions.solution_text:
$E \leftrightarrow S$ and $F \leftrightarrow T$, so side $EF$ corresponds to side $ST$.
$EF = 9$ cm
